convertibility_reason: Heavy pending order management with 3 simultaneous buy-stop/sell-stop orders, trailing stop logic modifying positions every tick, and dynamic order price modification based on StopLevel. The order modification loop with pending orders and tick-level trailing makes accurate Python backtesting difficult without tick data and order queue simulation.

other_exits: Trailing stop activates when price moves into profit beyond StopLevel+Spread from open price; SL moves to breakeven+Spread for buys or breakeven-Spread for sells, then trails by SL pips distance

position_sizing.conditional_logic: FreeMargin/2000, clamped to [0.1, 15], then divided by 3 for each of 3 pending orders

custom_logic_notes: EA places 3 identical pending buy-stop or sell-stop orders when RSI signal triggers. Pending order price is set at Ask+StopLevel (buy) or Bid-StopLevel (sell), not at a fixed offset. Pending orders are modified every tick: if order price is more than 20 points from current price, it is moved to Ask+20*_Point (buy-stop) or Bid-20*_Point (sell-stop). Trailing stop modifies SL on open positions when price has moved favorably beyond StopLevel+Spread from entry. The sell-stop modification block has a bug: it calls OrderSend twice (lines 204 and 207), sending a duplicate modify request. Entry uses RSI[1] (previous bar), not RSI[0] (current bar).
python_conversion_notes: Three main challenges: (1) Pending order queue management - 3 identical stop orders placed simultaneously, then modified every tick based on price distance. Must simulate order activation when price reaches pending price. (2) Trailing stop logic runs every tick and depends on StopLevel (broker variable) and Spread - both must be available in backtest data. (3) The sell-stop modification has a double OrderSend bug that would need to be corrected in Python. Position sizing depends on AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_FREEMARGIN) which requires equity tracking throughout the backtest. Recommend tick data with spread information for accurate backtesting.
